messages.subject: New to Shiny Modules
parts:
I have a somewhat complex app that I am trying to convert to Shiny modules.  I am not sure of the best way to post code to show the issue.  I am not sure what the problem is, but in a nutshell, I have a Shiny Module UI and Module Server.  These are called in ui.R and server.R respectively.

Normally, the way the app is constructed right now I have a tabset in a the main display.  Each tab contains a set of questions that have to be answered.  The number of tabs is changed depending on input$method.  The last tab uses the same set of questions for two selected methods.  So I have the code replicated with different ID's right now.  The app currently works.

Changing to modules, I have converted the same code into modules.  Likely I have not done something quite right, the tab in question will not populate based on the modules.  The other tabs are populating just fine using the old method.  The app is running and not showing any error codes.

The set of questions assigned to the tabs, along with the three possible answers, is kept in a csv file that is read in when the app is launched. Each question (4 for this tab) is displayed and a radiobutton is used to select among the answers. 

In the previous approach, I used dyanmicUI to generated the items to populate each tab.

My Module UI:

ImpactQuestInput <- function(id,label = "Impact Questions") {

  ns <- NS(id)

  uiOutput(ns("ImpactAction"))

}


My Module Server:

ImpactQuest <- function(input, output, session, questionSet) {
 
  ##### Create Question Labels
 
  labelQc01 <- renderText({
    paste("C01 : ",questionSet()[questionSet()$QID == 'C01',]$Element.Question,sep = "")
  })

  labelQc02 <- renderText({
    paste("C02 : ",questionSet()[questionSet()$QID == 'C02',]$Element.Question,sep = "")
  })
 
  labelQc03 <- renderText({
    paste("C03 : ",questionSet()[questionSet()$QID == 'C03',]$Element.Question,sep = "")
  })
 
  labelQc04 <- renderText({
    paste("C04 : ",questionSet()[questionSet()$QID == 'C04',]$Element.Question,sep = "")
  })
 
  ##### Create Radio Button Label List
 
  optionListc01 <- reactive({
    questionSet() <- questionSet()[1,5:ncol(questionSet())]
    # Remove items from the questionSet() if the option is empty.
    # Also, convert the option list to matrix.
    as.matrix(questionSet()[questionSet()!=""])
  })
 
  optionListc02 <- reactive({
    questionSet() <- questionSet()[2,5:ncol(questionSet())]
    # Remove items from the questionSet() if the option is empty.
    # Also, convert the option list to matrix.
    as.matrix(questionSet()[questionSet()!=""])
  })
 
  optionListc03 <- reactive({
    questionSet() <- questionSet()[3,5:ncol(questionSet())]
    # Remove items from the questionSet() if the option is empty.
    # Also, convert the option list to matrix.
    as.matrix(questionSet()[questionSet()!=""])
  })
 
  optionListc04 <- reactive({
    questionSet() <- questionSet()[4,5:ncol(questionSet())]
    # Remove items from the questionSet() if the option is empty.
    # Also, convert the option list to matrix.
    as.matrix(questionSet()[questionSet()!=""])
  })
 
  dynamicUiInputsImpact <- reactive({
    if (input$method == "1") {
      return(
        list(
          h4(textOutput("labelQc01")),
          radioButtons(ns("c1"), "Please Select:",
                       c(optionListc01())
          ),
          tags$hr(style="border-color: darkblue;"),
          h4(textOutput("labelQc02")),
          radioButtons(ns("c2"), "Please Select:",
                       c(optionListc02())
          ),
          tags$hr(style="border-color: darkblue;"),
          h4(textOutput("labelQc03")),
          radioButtons(ns("c3"), "Please Select:",
                       c(optionListc03())
          ),
          tags$hr(style="border-color: darkblue;"),
          h4(textOutput("labelQc04")),
          radioButtons(ns("c4"), "Please Select:",
                       c(optionListc04())
          )
        )
      )
    }
  })
 
  output$ImpactAction <- renderUI( {
    dynamicUiInputsImpact()
  })

}

My UI call:

    mainPanel(
      navbarPage("Select:",
                 tabPanel("Inputs",
                          fluidPage("inputs",
                                    # input.level is the tab number
                                    # input.method is the method switch for quick, partial and full quantitative
                                    uiOutput("tabs"),
                                    ...                                                                                                          #(other conditional panels)
                                    conditionalPanel(condition = "input.level == 3 && input.method == 1",
                                                    ImpactQuestInput("ImpactQList1")
                                    ),
                                   ...                                                                                                          #(other conditional panels)
                      ...        )                                                                                                  #(other tabpanels)
        ...       )
)                                                                                                   #(other navbar items)

My server call:

  observe({
    if (input$method == 1) callModule(ImpactQuest,"ImpactQlist1",questionSet)
  })

messages.subject: Re: New to Shiny Modules
parts:
Well, it's definitely harder to get help online when you have a large and/or proprietary app. Here's a great article with general tips, including how to make a minimal reproducible example (MRE). In you case, this means having a minimal module and minimal app code, just enough to show the problem. Crucially, it has to be copy-pasteable and runnable. The longer I have to spend getting your code to even run, the less time I'll have to actually help. It also helps a lot to have data that is copy-pasteable (in this case, an in-memory data frame or tibble), rather than making me download a file. That takes care of the large part. The proprietary part requires you to create dummy data with the same structure.

I'll try to take a look at this later today, but if you can get a better MRE, that will go a long way.

parts:
I think I found your issue though. It's a simple typo.

In the UI, you call the module and give it an id "ImpactQList1": 

ImpactQuestInput("ImpactQList1")
 
However, when you call the server module, you use a different id: "ImpactQlist1" (notice that lowercase l, when it should have been an uppercase L)

callModule(ImpactQuest,"ImpactQlist1",questionSet)

So, you see, in this case, there was no problem with the code logic and the issue was a simple typo. The problem asking for help without a runnable example is precisely this. I ended up spending a lot more time making the code runnable than the time I took to find the bug. So you have an idea of what a MRE would look like for this situation, here's what I got:


# ------------------------------------ MODULE ----------------------------------
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# module UI
modUI <- function(id) {
  ns <- NS(id)
  
  tagList(
    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc01"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c1"), "Please Select:", choices = c("")),
    tags$hr(style = "border-color: darkblue;"),
    
    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc02"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c2"), "Please Select:", choices = c("")),
    tags$hr(style = "border-color: darkblue;"),
    
    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc03"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c3"), "Please Select:", choices = c("")),
    tags$hr(style = "border-color: darkblue;"),
    
    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc04"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c4"), "Please Select:", choices = c(""))
  )
}

# module server
mod <- function(input, output, session, questionSet) {
  
  createLabel <- function(name) {
    paste0(name, ": ", 
      questionSet[questionSet$QID == name,]$Element.Question,
      sep = "")
  }
  
  output$labelQc01 <- renderText({ createLabel("C01") })
  output$labelQc02 <- renderText({ createLabel("C02") })
  output$labelQc03 <- renderText({ createLabel("C03") })
  output$labelQc04 <- renderText({ createLabel("C04") })
  
  createOptions <- function(row) {
    as.character(questionSet[row,5:ncol(questionSet)])
  }
  
  updateRadioButtons(session, "c1", choices = createOptions(1))
  updateRadioButtons(session, "c2", choices = createOptions(2))
  updateRadioButtons(session, "c3", choices = createOptions(3))
  updateRadioButtons(session, "c4", choices = createOptions(4))
}

library(shiny)

questionSet <- tibble::tibble(
  QID = c("C01", "C02", "C03", "C04"),
  Element.Question = c(
    "Do you like icecream?",
    "Do you like sunny days?",
    "Do you like going to the movies?",
    "Do you like coffee?"
  ),
  col3 = c(character(1), character(1), character(1), character(1)),
  col4 = c(character(1), character(1), character(1), character(1)),
  Option1 = c("Yes", "Yes", "Yes", "Yes"),
  Option2 = c("No", "No", "No", "No"),
  Option3 = c("Maybe", "Maybe", "Maybe", "Maybe")
)

ui <- navbarPage("Select:",
  tabPanel("Inputs", modUI("questions"))
) 

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  callModule(mod, "questions", questionSet = questionSet)
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
